notes: Circuit: a multi-stage discrete bipolar network drawn across the whole sheet, fed by four separate supply-arrow taps (+15V at the top, +10V, +6V and +5V) with a common ground rail along the bottom (y~808) that carries the GND symbol #22 at (883,770). I read the drawing first at 4x and 12x zoom before looking at the tracer output; the skeleton topology it found matches my reading, but five of the nine transistors had their collector/emitter (or base/emitter) terminal order wrong, which is what most of this annotation fixes. NET MAP (23 components, 16 nets; labels as emitted by finalize.py): n1 = the +15V top rail - the +15V arrow #0, top of the 15k resistor #1, and the collector of NPN #3. n2 = the node between the two 15k resistors #1 and #5 on the left column, where the +10V arrow #2 taps in at (245,310). n3 = base of NPN #3 and the upper terminal of diode #4 (a short link at y~306). n4 = the +5V rail - emitter of NPN #3, the +5V arrow #6, the right end of 15k #8, the emitter of PNP #12 and the collector of NPN #17; it is the big solder-dot node at (824,442) plus the vertical down to (824,512). n5 = the isolated column between diode #4 (lower terminal) and diode #10 (upper terminal); this column hops over the horizontal mid-rail at (763,445). n6 = the node at (255,461) - bottom of 15k #5, left end of the 180Omega resistor #9, and the EMITTER of PNP #11. n7 = the +6V node at (457,454) - the +6V arrow #7, right end of 180Omega #9, left end of 15k #8, and the EMITTER of PNP #13. n8 = lower terminal of diode #10, the BASE of PNP #12 and the COLLECTOR of NPN #21 (dot at (745,576), then the long wire east/south to (700,724)). n9 = COLLECTOR of PNP #11 down the x~255 column to the COLLECTOR of NPN #19. n10 = BASE of PNP #11 (left lead at (222,541), west to x~180 then south) and the EMITTER of PNP #16. n11 = COLLECTOR of PNP #12 and the BASE of NPN #17. n12 = COLLECTOR of PNP #13, COLLECTOR of NPN #20 (dot at (462,682)) and the BASE of NPN #21, reached by the wire that steps east, south to y~760 and east again under the S47 hop. n13 = BASE of PNP #13 and the top of the 50k resistor #15. n14 = the input node - the bare up-arrow source #14 at (87,592), the BASE of PNP #16, and the top of the 50Omega resistor #18 (junction at (90,647)). n15 = BASE of NPN #19 and BASE of NPN #20, the lone horizontal at y~748 between (295,738) and (423,753). 0 = the bottom rail and GND - bottom of 50k #15, COLLECTOR of PNP #16, EMITTER of NPN #17, bottom of 50Omega #18, emitters of NPN #19/#20/#21, and GND #22. CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all 16 inspected in the crops; the two hops were additionally checked at 4x on the raw scan): S3 (528,231) JUNCTION - the +15V arrow's stub terminates on the top rail, a clean T; otherwise the supply symbol would sit on a one-terminal net. S7 (245,310) JUNCTION - the +10V feed arrives from the left and meets the left column between the two 15k resistors, a clean T. S13 (824,442) JUNCTION - a genuine filled solder dot (dot metric 3.2, i.e. ~3x stroke width in both axes, plainly visible as a blob in the crop) at the 4-way where the vertical from NPN #3's emitter, the 15k #8 rail from the west and the +5V tap from the east meet. Reading it as a crossing would sever the +5V tap from #12/#17 and leave #8's right end floating. S14 (763,445) CROSSING - the diode #4-to-#10 column makes an unmistakable semicircular hop around the horizontal mid-rail (hop metric 20.2; the S-bend is obvious at 4x). Reading it as a junction would tie the diode string to the +6V/+5V rail and short both diodes out, and would also merge n5 into n4/n7. S16 (457,454) JUNCTION - solder dot (dot 3.2) at the 4-way where the +6V arrow, the 180Omega rail from the west, the 15k rail to the east and the drop to PNP #13's emitter meet. S17 (255,461) JUNCTION - clean T: the left column runs continuously from 15k #5 down to PNP #11's emitter and the 180Omega rail branches east; not joining it would strand the 180Omega rail. S18 (824,512) JUNCTION - three-way corner on the +5V column: down from (824,442), east then south to NPN #17's collector, and south-west to PNP #12's emitter. All three are drawn meeting at one corner. S23 (745,576) JUNCTION - solder dot (2.9) where the diode #10 column continues south and a stub runs east to PNP #12's base. S35 (90,647) JUNCTION - T on the input column: source #14 above, 50Omega #18 below, stub east to PNP #16's base. S36 (462,682) JUNCTION - dot (2.5) where PNP #13's collector column continues down to NPN #20's collector and a wire leaves east toward NPN #21's base. S47 (585,759) CROSSING - clear semicircular hop (hop 15.4): the 50k #15 bottom lead descends and bulges around the horizontal wire that carries n12 east to NPN #21's base. Reading it as a junction would tie the 50k's grounded end to n12, shorting the 50k and merging n12 with ground. S50 (179,804), S51 (686,807), S52 (251,808), S53 (565,812), S54 (470,816) all JUNCTION - each is a lead terminating on the bottom ground rail (PNP #16 collector, NPN #21 emitter, NPN #19 emitter, 50k #15 bottom, NPN #20 emitter); S51/S52/S53 carry visible solder dots (2.7/2.9/2.9). In every case the branch has a free end, so any other reading would strand a terminal on a one-terminal net. NON-CRITICAL SITES left at default: S0/S2 (the '+15V' and '15kOhm' labels touching the rail and resistor #1), S5/S8 ('+10V'), S9/S10 ('+6V'), S11 ('+5V'), S24/S26/S27/S28/S30/S34 ('50kOhm' brushing resistor #15), S37/S41/S42 ('50Ohm' brushing resistor #18), S46 (878,741) which is the already-net-0 node where NPN #17's emitter, the ground rail and the GND stub meet. All 16 gap bridges sit in label ink and none changes the netlist. PIN-ORDER FIXES (the substantive correction on this sheet). The drafter is completely consistent: every PNP is drawn with the emitter arrow on the lead nearer the supply, pointing INTO the base bar, and every NPN with the emitter arrow on the lead nearer ground, pointing AWAY from the base bar. I checked all nine transistors individually at 12x. The tracer had defaulted every 3-terminal part to (top, side, bottom) = (t0,t1,t2), which is right for the NPNs here but inverts collector and emitter on all four PNPs. #11 BJT-PNP (248,541): arrowhead sits on the UPPER lead with its vertex against the base bar, so emitter = p1 (255,501, up to n6), base = p0 (222,541, left), collector = p2 (253,581, down to NPN #19's collector). Remapped t0->p2, t1->p0, t2->p1. Physical check agrees: a PNP must have its emitter at the more positive node, and n6 (the 15k/15k divider off +15V) is well above n9. #12 BJT-PNP (804,577): same geometry, arrow on the upper lead pointing down-left into the bar. Emitter = p1 (813,532) on the +5V rail, base = p0 (773,572), collector = p2 (817,620) driving NPN #17's base. Remapped t0->p2, t1->p0, t2->p1. #13 BJT-PNP (473,581): mirrored - base bar on the right, leads to the left. Arrowhead vertex points down-right into the bar on the UPPER lead, so emitter = p0 (458,535) on the +6V node, base = p2 (504,576, right, to the 50k), collector = p1 (460,626) down to n12. Remapped t0->p1, t1->p2, t2->p0. #16 BJT-PNP (168,641): arrow on the UPPER lead into the bar, so emitter = p1 (179,598) up to PNP #11's base, base = p2 (139,644, left, the input node), collector = p0 (175,682) down to the ground rail. Remapped t0->p0, t1->p2, t2->p1. This is a PNP emitter follower with its collector on the negative rail; the opposite reading (emitter on ground, collector at n10) would need n10 below ground to conduct, which is impossible in this all-positive-supply circuit. #21 BJT-NPN (663,752): here the error was base vs emitter, not collector vs emitter. The base lead is the horizontal one leaving the bar to the WEST at (625,757) (wire 37, running back to n12); the big '>' arrowhead is on the lower-right lead at (684,793), which drops onto the ground rail, so that is the emitter; the upper-right lead (700,724, wire 189) is the collector going to n8. The tracer had t1=p2 and t2=p1, i.e. base and emitter swapped. Remapped t0->p0, t1->p1, t2->p2. The other four transistors were already right and were left alone after verification: #3 (811,314) NPN collector=p1 top to +15V, base=p2 left to diode #4, emitter=p0 bottom to +5V (arrow on the lower lead pointing away from the bar); #17 (863,692) NPN collector=p0 top to +5V, base=p2 left, emitter=p1 bottom to ground; #19 (267,741) NPN (mirrored) collector=p1 upper-left, base=p0 right, emitter=p2 lower-left to ground; #20 (453,756) NPN collector=p0 top, base=p2 left, emitter=p1 bottom to ground. CLASSES: I believe all 23 are correct as annotated. The four supply arrows are V-DC (one port) as labelled, the two triangle-and-bar symbols at (752,349) and (746,501) are Diodes, the zig-zags are Resistors, and the NPN/PNP split matches the arrow directions I read at 12x in every case. OPEN POINT (not resolvable from the drawing, recorded rather than fixed): net n15 - the wire at y~748 joining the base of NPN #19 to the base of NPN #20 - touches only those two terminals. I zoomed (355,750) at 8x and confirmed nothing else attaches anywhere along it: it is a single unbroken stroke from (283,743) to (423,753) with no stub, dot or crossing. So the drafter really did leave that base pair undriven. GT records the drawing, so I have left it as a two-terminal net rather than inventing a connection.
